name: Make your own environment
line: Pick how unstable the air is and how much the wind changes with height; see which storm it makes.
note: Temperature and moisture follow Weisman and Klemp (1982), CM1's own analytic sounding, with the moisture near the ground set for your instability; the wind is calm at the ground and changes by your shear over the lowest 6 km, turning as in CM1's supercell case. The view follows the storm your air makes. The area is not made smaller than 120 km, because CM1's parcel grid covers 120 km; the fit makes the grid coarser or the storm shorter instead.

changes.why: a picture every 5 minutes, so the live view moves
netCDF, which ncview, xarray and most tools read (CM1's file asks for GrADS)
one file per saved time, so each picture has its own file
the sounding is the file input_sounding beside this namelist
the wind comes from the sounding file (CM1 sets iwnd = 0 with isnd = 7)
follow air parcels, so Results can show air rising into the storm
CM1's own parcel grid: 60 x 60 across, every 2 km, and 10 levels, every 1 km
the moving frame follows the storm this sounding makes (the storm-track check's recommended frame)
the moving frame follows the storm this sounding makes (the storm-track check's recommended frame)

gm1_settings_why: The warm bubble that starts the storm sits 6.3 km east and 7 km south of the centre, the storm-track check's recommended place for this sounding, so the storm keeps the most room to every side. CM1 keeps the bubble in its code, not the namelist, so this is a GM1 setting.

sounding.rights: written by GM1 (gpuwm-cm1 preset environment) from Weisman and Klemp's (1982) formulas as CM1 r21.1 base.F transcribes them

environment.method: Weisman and Klemp (1982) temperature and moisture as CM1 r21.1 base.F isnd = 5 builds them, with the boundary-layer mixing-ratio cap set for the CAPE target; wind calm at the ground with the chosen 0-6 km shear (curved: CM1's iwnd = 2 shape, scaled)
